title: Hypertension fuels osteoarthritis through neuroendocrine signaling.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no text-mined accessions); NCBI elink from PubMed 42821663 returned only related-article links, no GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample/dbGaP; GEO searches for chondrocyte+vasopressin/AVPR1A/NR4A3 returned one unrelated 2019-era series (GSE136198); a listing of the 20 most recent osteoarthritis GEO series (Aug-Oct 2026) contains nothing matching this study; the Science article page and its supplementary PDF both return HTTP 403; PubMed XML record contains no DataBank/AccessionNumber entries.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the study design comes from the abstract plus a press summary: a nationwide analysis of 36,820 Korean adults aged 45+ from KNHANES (Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey), hypertensive mouse models, chondrocyte transcriptomic profiling, and gene-silencing experiments. I never saw a single data file, row count, column, or unit.

a1_downloadable.note: No data from this paper is reachable. The article and its supplementary materials sit behind a Science paywall (HTTP 403), there is no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports no supplementary files, and no GEO, SRA, BioProject or other repository deposit is linked from PubMed or findable by keyword search. The only named data source, KNHANES, is a separate Korean government survey requiring registration and a data-use agreement on its own portal, not a file attached to this paper.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Cannot be assessed because no file exists to inspect. The plausible labels (radiographic knee osteoarthritis grade in the survey; mouse cartilage damage scores) would have to be pulled from a third-party survey or from figure-level histology scores that are not released as a table.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table of any kind was located; transcriptomic count matrices are not deposited in any repository I could find.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checkable without files; the abstract names no measured quantity with units.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown. The 36,820 survey participants belong to KNHANES, not to this paper; the paper's own experiments are mouse and cell experiments whose n is typically single-digit to low-double-digit per group.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown, likely under 1 GB if any table existed
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size would not be the problem; availability is.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No download exists to compare with the paper's stated counts.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. The clinical label (radiographic osteoarthritis grade) is a human read in KNHANES, which would be fine, but it is not in any file released with this paper.

existing_models.name: Machine-learning models for knee osteoarthritis progression (a large published family, summarised in a 2025 Journal of Medical Internet Research systematic review and meta-analysis, found by web search)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified by me. The review reports that these models show 'certain discriminatory power' and that 90.6% of studies train on the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) cohort and 18.8% on the Multicenter Osteoarthritis Study, with heterogeneous progression definitions and weak external validation.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: The review names standardising the definition of osteoarthritis progression and stringent external validation as the unsolved parts.

integration.partner_dataset: Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) and GTEx/Human Protein Atlas for AVPR1A expression
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID for the expression side; no shared key exists on the clinical side because no per-participant data is released
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does blood-pressure status add predictive power to existing knee-osteoarthritis progression models beyond age, sex and body mass index? — a real question, but one that needs OAI, not this paper, because this paper releases nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: Would have been: recover the known association of body mass index and age with osteoarthritis grade. Not testable without data.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling. Not testable without data.
controls.external_validation: Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) would serve, but it is a different dataset entirely.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases no data file, so nothing can be modelled or verified from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use blood pressure and routine health-survey measures to predict how damaged a person's knee cartilage is.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would have used each survey participant's blood pressure, age, sex, body mass index and blood chemistry; the paper mentions 36,820 adults, but those records belong to the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, not to any file released here, so the usable count is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: The radiographic osteoarthritis grade of the knee, read by a radiologist from an X-ray using the standard Kellgren-Lawrence 0-4 scale. That reading exists only inside the Korean survey, which must be requested separately.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: If blood pressure genuinely adds information beyond weight and age, rheumatologists and primary-care doctors already measure it at every visit, so risk stratification would cost nothing extra. Even a null result would tell the field the newly reported hormone pathway does not translate into a usable risk signal.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes no accessible data at all. The clinical analysis reuses a public Korean survey, and knee-osteoarthritis prediction models are already trained on the much larger, imaging-rich Osteoarthritis Initiative cohort.

confidence_score.why: Per-prediction confidence needs replicate or repeated measurements per person; nothing of the kind is released, and I could not inspect any file.

models_beatable.why: Dozens of knee-osteoarthritis progression models published through 2025 use imaging plus clinical variables; a blood-pressure-only addition to survey covariates would not beat them, and I have no data to try.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: there is no dataset here to join, no join key, and no baseline we could run on the same split.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The nearest defensible project — testing whether blood pressure improves knee-osteoarthritis risk prediction — would have to be run on the Osteoarthritis Initiative cohort or on a KNHANES extract obtained independently, and would be a re-analysis inspired by this paper rather than a project built on its data.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data file was obtainable, so there is nothing to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Ask whether any repository accession is attached to the paper. Done in the first ten minutes: PubMed's elink returns no GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample or dbGaP record, and the supplement is paywalled. That single check kills it.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails: a paywalled Science paper with no PubMed Central copy, no supplementary files retrievable, and no deposited dataset findable in GEO, SRA, BioProject or any other repository. The one named data source, the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, is a third-party resource needing its own registration and is not this paper's data. Nothing can be verified, so the remaining checklist parts were not scored.
